problem: RAG behaviour on narrow financial corpora such as regulatory and procedural documents is understudied; no existing systematic comparison of retrieval paradigms for such corpora (statement limited to this corpus).
method: A 100-question, manually verified domain benchmark over 33 central-bank payment system reports; structure-aware chunking; comparison of four conditions (zero-context, BM25, dense bge-small-en-v1.5, hybrid BM25+dense RRF) with generation by llama-3.3-70b-instruct.
key_assumptions: The corpus is static (no document versioning or amendment relations)
main_contribution: First systematic sparse/dense/hybrid retrieval comparison for regulatory financial documents on an RMA (Bhutan) corpora benchmark, with open benchmark and evaluation code.
datasets: 33 Royal Monetary Authority of Bhutan payment system reports (2018-2026), 1,033 pages, 1,456 tables, 2,869 structure-aware chunks
100 domain questions across factual, numerical, trend and multihop categories
baselines: Hybrid BM25+dense with Reciprocal Rank Fusion
results: Hybrid achieves the best overall performance (ROUGE-L 0.513, BERTScore F1 0.697, faithfulness 90.0%, no-answer rate 16%), beating BM25-only (+17.4% ROUGE-L) and dense-only (+19.3% ROUGE-L); BM25 beats hybrid on multihop queries (ROUGE-L 0.304 vs 0.239).
limitations: Single institution corpus (Bhutan central bank), limited generalization
Questions have no target date, so document time or version is not modelled
Hybrid RRF underperforms BM25 on multihop queries
code_availability: Public: https://github.com/PravaatChhetri/rma-rag-benchmark (verified via inspect_repository: Jupyter notebook pipeline, pinned requirements.txt, ROUGE/BERTScore computed live, benchmark CSV with example rows)

relation_to_idea.conceptual_difference: A static regulatory-document QA benchmark with no temporal dimension, no version timestamps, and no query target dates; it supplies baseline retrieval configurations and an evaluation harness rather than a temporal relevance component, and it does not address supersession or overlapping revisions.
relation_to_idea.basis: Abstract describes a sparse/dense/hybrid comparison on a static report corpus with answer-quality metrics; timestamps and versioning are absent.
